text: お会いできて嬉しいです。 / ガードまで勤めていただいて、どうお礼をしたらいいのか。
translation: I'm so happy to meet you. / You've even served as my guardian — I don't know how to thank you.

vocabulary.meaning: to serve, to work (in a role)

grammar: 〜ていただいて uses the te-form of いただく (humble form of もらう), expressing grateful receipt of someone's action. どうお礼をしたらいいのか is an indirect question meaning 'I don't know how I should express my thanks.'

text: いいえ、俺はシンを倒すこと
translation: No — for me, it's about defeating Sin.
grammar: The sentence ends abruptly with こと, a nominalizer, leaving the predicate unspoken — a dramatic pause common in game dialogue, implying 'defeating Sin is [all that matters / my purpose].'

text: そうですよね / はい、私はシンを倒します
translation: That's right, isn't it. / Yes — I will defeat Sin.
grammar: そうですよね combines そう (so/that way), です (polite copula), よ (assertive particle), and ね (agreement-seeking particle). The combination softens the statement into a gentle affirmation seeking agreement.

text: みんながこれを見る頃にはシンはもういないでしょう
translation: By the time everyone sees this, Sin will already be gone.

vocabulary.meaning: around the time of, by the time

grammar: 〜頃には marks a future reference point ('by the time ~'). でしょう at the end expresses confident conjecture — Yuna is recording a message to be seen after Sin's defeat.

text: それに、私も
translation: And also… me too.

vocabulary.meaning: furthermore, and also, on top of that

grammar: The sentence trails off without a predicate — a deliberate ellipsis. Yuna begins to say she will also be gone (dead), but cannot finish the thought. The incompleteness itself carries emotional weight.

text: だから今のうちに言っておきます / アーロンさん
translation: That's why I want to say it now, while I still can. / Auron.

vocabulary.meaning: while there's still time, now while I can
to do in advance, to do and leave done

grammar: 今のうちに is an idiom meaning 'while the opportunity exists / while there's still time.' 〜ておきます (te-form + おく, polite) indicates doing something as preparation or leaving it done for later.

text: ありがとうございます
translation: Thank you very much.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございます
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございます

grammar: The full formal expression of gratitude. ありがとう is the base; ございます is the formal/humble form of ある. Used for sincere, heartfelt thanks in formal or emotional contexts.

text: きまり
translation: Kimahri.
grammar: A one-word utterance — simply addressing Kimahri by name. In Japanese, directly naming someone can function as a call or an emotional acknowledgment, here part of Yuna's recorded farewells.

text: 初めて会った日のこと覚えてる?
translation: Do you remember the day we first met?
grammar: 〜のこと after a noun phrase turns it into the object of 覚えてる ('remember about / remember the matter of'). 覚えてる is the contracted te-iru form, indicating a continuing state of memory.

text: 私が七つの時だよ / 父さんがシンを倒して
translation: I was seven years old. / Father had just defeated Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: seven (native Japanese counting, used for age)

grammar: 七つ is the native Japanese word for 'seven,' traditionally used to express a child's age. The sentence 父さんがシンを倒して ends with the te-form, acting as a subordinate clause ('having defeated Sin') that connects to the next sentence.

text: レベルは大騒ぎでね / みんなが父さんを褒めたたえて
translation: Luca was in an uproar. / Everyone was praising Father.
grammar: 大騒ぎでね uses で (te-form of the copula だ) + ね (softening particle), describing the state with a casual, reminiscing tone. 褒めたたえて is again the te-form, continuing the sequence of recollections.

text: 自分のことみたいに嬉しかった / でも夜になって思ったんだ
translation: I was happy as if it were my own achievement. / But when night came, I started thinking.

vocabulary.meaning: was happy (past tense of 嬉しい)

grammar: 自分のことみたいに literally means 'as if it were about myself.' みたいに is a casual comparison particle (like ように but colloquial). 〜んだ at the end adds an explanatory, reflective nuance.

text: シンを倒したけど
translation: He defeated Sin, but…

vocabulary.meaning: but, although (often leaves the following clause implied)

grammar: 〜けど here is a concessive conjunction used to leave an implication hanging — the full thought ('Sin was defeated, but Father died') is not completed, creating emotional suspense.

text: 父さん死んじゃったんだ / 私一人ぼっちなんだって眠れなくて
translation: Father was gone. / I couldn't sleep, telling myself I was all alone.

vocabulary.meaning: died (contraction of 死んでしまった, regretful nuance)
to be able to sleep (potential form of 眠る)

grammar: 〜ちゃった (contraction of てしまった) conveys a regrettable or irreversible completion. 〜なんだって is a reported inner thought: 'telling myself that [I was alone].' 眠れなくて ends with the te-form of the negative potential, linking cause and consequence.

text: そのまま街に出て / お祭り騒ぎを抜けて
translation: Just as I was, I went out into the city / and slipped through the festival crowd.

vocabulary.meaning: just as it is, unchanged, without doing anything different
to slip through, to pass through, to exit

grammar: A chain of te-forms (出て, 抜けて) strings together sequential actions in narrative style — characteristic of storytelling in Japanese. そのまま indicates she went out in her current state (without changing anything).

text: レベルの長い橋に立って / 一人で眺めてた
translation: I stood on the long bridge in Luca / and gazed out alone.

vocabulary.meaning: to gaze at, to look out at

grammar: 眺めてた is a contraction of 眺めていた (te-iru in past tense), indicating a continuous action in the past. The image of standing alone on a bridge gazing out evokes loneliness and reflection.

text: 父さんを見送った橋から
translation: From the same bridge where I saw Father off…

vocabulary.meaning: to see off, to watch someone leave; also to farewell the dead

grammar: 見送った is the past-tense modifier of 見送る, modifying 橋 ('the bridge from which I saw him off'). The sentence ends with から, leaving the clause hanging — what she saw from that bridge is described in the next line.

text: 父さんが戦った平原を
translation: …the plains where Father had fought.
grammar: 父さんが戦った modifies 平原 — a relative clause in Japanese precedes the noun it modifies. The sentence ends with を (object particle), completing the image of gazing across the plains where the battle took place.

text: そしたらキマリが現れたんだ / ブラスカの娘を探しているって言ったでしょ
translation: And then Kimahri appeared. / He said he was looking for Braska's daughter, remember?

vocabulary.meaning: and then, and when that happened (casual)
to search for, to look for

grammar: 〜て言ったでしょ combines the quotation marker って with the verb 言った (said) and the confirmation-seeking でしょ. Yuna is speaking directly to Kimahri, invoking a shared memory.

text: 最初は怖かった
translation: At first I was scared.
grammar: 最初は uses は as a topic/contrast marker, implying 'at first [I was scared], but later…' The は sets up a contrast with what follows. 怖かった is the plain past tense of the い-adjective 怖い.

text: でもすぐにわかったよ優しい人なんだって
translation: But I quickly understood — that you were a kind person.
grammar: 優しい人なんだって combines the explanatory なんだ with って (quotation), expressing the content of her realization: 'I understood [the fact] that he's a kind person.' The inner realization is quoted with って.

text: 子供と話すの慣れてなかったんだよね
translation: You just weren't used to talking with children, were you.

vocabulary.meaning: to get used to, to become accustomed to

grammar: 〜のは nominalization: 話すの = 'the act of talking.' 慣れてなかった is the negative te-iru past ('wasn't accustomed'). んだよね is a combined sentence-final that adds explanation (んだ) + assertion (よ) + shared understanding (ね).

text: 私がブラスカの娘ですって答えたら
translation: When I answered that I was Braska's daughter,
grammar: 〜って答えたら uses the quotation って inside a たら conditional/temporal clause. 答えたら = 'when I answered.' The result of that action is described in the next line.

text: ベベルから一番遠いところへ私を連れて行くって
translation: He said he would take me to the farthest place from Bevelle.

vocabulary.meaning: to take someone along, to bring with

grammar: ベベルから一番遠いところ = 'the place farthest from Bevelle.' 〜って at the end is a casual quotation marker indicating reported speech: 'he said [that he would take me].'

text: これは死に行く者の願いだって
translation: He said it was the wish of one going to their death.

vocabulary.meaning: to go to one's death, to go forth to die

grammar: 死に行く者 uses 死に行く (compound verb: to go to die) as a relative clause modifying 者. The whole phrase 〜だって again indicates reported speech. This refers to Braska's dying wish passed through Kimahri.

text: 私泣いちゃったよね
translation: I ended up crying, didn't I.
grammar: 泣いちゃった is a contraction of 泣いてしまった — the て-form of 泣く + しまった, expressing that something happened completely, often with emotional weight (regret or surprise). よね seeks shared recollection.

text: あれはね
translation: That was because…

vocabulary.meaning: that (referring to something in the past or distant)
as for ~ (は topic marker + ね soft/reflective particle)

grammar: あれはね picks up the previous topic ('that moment of crying') and signals an explanation is coming. The ね adds a soft, intimate tone — Yuna is about to share something personal.

text: 父さんが死んだんだって / もう会えないんだって分かったから
translation: It's because I realized that Father was dead — that I could never see him again.

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to meet (potential form of 会う)

grammar: 〜んだって + 分かった = 'I realized [the fact] that ~.' The double 〜んだって structure (once for 死んだ, once for 会えない) piles up painful realizations. 〜から provides the reason for her crying.

text: キマリ何も言わずに抱きしめてくれた
translation: Kimahri hugged me without saying a word.

vocabulary.meaning: to do (something) for me (expressing gratitude for another's action)

grammar: 何も言わずに uses the ずに negative form of 言う ('without saying') as an adverbial. 〜てくれた adds the nuance that Kimahri did this for Yuna's sake — a deeply appreciative framing.

text: リサイドに着いてからも私泣いたっけ / 私をジーンに預けたらキマリ村を出ようとしたじゃない
translation: Even after arriving in Besaid, I kept crying. / And when he left me with Jiin, Kimahri tried to leave the village, didn't he.

vocabulary.meaning: to leave in someone's care, to entrust
to try to do, to be about to do

grammar: 着いてからも = 'even after arriving.' 〜たら is temporal ('when he did'). 〜ようとした captures an attempted action. じゃない at the end is a soft, familiar confirmation-seeking form, like 'right?' in reminiscing.

text: 行かないでってしがみついて泣いた
translation: I clung to him crying, begging 'Don't go.'

vocabulary.meaning: please don't go (request not to do)
to cling to, to grab onto

grammar: 行かないでって quotes Yuna's plea using the casual quotation marker って. しがみついて is the te-form showing simultaneous action: 'clinging and crying.' The sequence paints a vivid scene of a child's desperation.

text: あれからずっとそばにいてくれて
translation: And since then, he's always been by my side.

vocabulary.meaning: since then, from that point on
all along, continuously, the whole time
to be by one's side, to be near

grammar: あれから marks a temporal origin point ('from that moment onward'). ずっと intensifies the continuity. いてくれて is the te-form of いてくれる, which itself expresses grateful receipt — the sentence trails off with emotional gratitude.

text: ひまり
translation: Kimahri.
grammar: A tender variant pronunciation of キマリ — Yuna says his name softly, with deep emotion after recounting their years together. The slight phonetic softening (ひまり for キマリ) reflects the intimacy of the moment.

text: 本当に
translation: Truly.
grammar: A standalone adverb used as an emphatic utterance — 'truly (thank you),' the predicate being implied. This kind of ellipsis is common in emotional speech where the feeling itself is communicated by the word alone.

text: ありがとう / 折れた角
translation: Thank you. / Your broken horn.
grammar: 折れた角 is a nominal phrase ('the broken horn') — a reference to Kimahri's broken horn, a visible mark of his past. Used here as a term of endearment, addressing Kimahri by this characteristic feature.

text: 好きだよ
translation: I love you.

vocabulary.meaning: to like, to love (can express deep affection depending on context)

grammar: 好きだよ directed at Kimahri in this emotional context expresses deep familial love and gratitude. よ adds warmth and gentle assertion. This is one of the most emotionally loaded lines of the campfire scene.

text: ワッカさん
translation: Wakka.
grammar: Addressing Wakka with さん shows polite respect — Yuna treats him as a trusted elder figure. In context, this is the start of her farewell words to Wakka.

text: ルール / リサイドで暮らした日々
translation: Lulu. / The days we lived in Besaid.

vocabulary.meaning: to live, to spend one's days

grammar: ルールー is shortened to ルール in speech — a casual nickname. リサイドで暮らした日々 is a noun phrase ('the days lived in Besaid') without an explicit predicate, evoking nostalgia by simply naming the memory.

text: ずっと忘れない / チャップさんと / 三人でよく遊んでくれた
translation: I'll never forget them. / With Chappu. / The three of you used to play with me so often.
grammar: 忘れない is the plain negative non-past — a strong, direct statement 'I will not forget.' 遊んでくれた uses くれた (past of くれる) to express that their playing was done for Yuna's benefit, adding warmth and gratitude.

text: だから
translation: That's why…
grammar: だから alone acts as a pivot — 'because of all that…' — building anticipation for the admission that follows. The pause after だから gives it emotional weight.

text: 召喚師になるって言った時
translation: When I said I was going to become a summoner,
grammar: 召喚師になるって is a nominalized quoted action ('saying I'd become a summoner'). 〜た時 sets up a temporal clause: 'at the time when I said it.'

text: あんなに反対してたのに / ごめんなさい / いつか謝ろうと思ってた
translation: You opposed it so strongly. / I'm sorry. / I'd always meant to apologize someday.

vocabulary.meaning: so much like that, to that extent
to intend to do, to think about doing

grammar: 〜てたのに (contraction of ていたのに) expresses contrast with a hint of reproach or sadness: 'even though [you] had been opposing it…' いつか謝ろうと思ってた = 'I had been thinking I would someday apologize' — an unfulfilled intention now finally spoken.

text: でもね
translation: But you know…
grammar: でもね is a soft pivot — 'but, you know…' The ね softens the contrast and invites the listener to lean in. Yuna is about to reveal something counterintuitive about how she felt.

text: 反対された時
translation: When you opposed me,

vocabulary.meaning: to be opposed, to face opposition (passive form)

grammar: 反対された is the passive form of 反対する: 'to be opposed.' The passive here centers Yuna as the recipient of that opposition — she was the one who faced it. 〜た時 sets up a temporal clause.

text: とても嬉しかったんだ / 私のこと
translation: I was actually very happy. / About me —
grammar: んだ adds an explanatory nuance — Yuna is revealing the real feeling behind the surface situation. 私のこと trails off, anticipating the explanation in the next line ('you were worried about me').

text: 心配してくれてるんだなって / 本当に兄さんと姉さんができたみたいだった
translation: I realized you were worried about me. / It really felt like I'd gained a big brother and sister.

vocabulary.meaning: to come to have, to gain (in terms of relationships)
it was like, it felt like (past)

grammar: 心配してくれてるんだなって is an inner realization quoted: 'I understood [the fact] that you were worried about me.' 兄さんと姉さんができた uses できる in the sense of 'a sibling came into existence [for me]' — a natural expression for gaining family.

text: ううん、本当の兄さんと姉さんだと思ってる
translation: No — I think of you as my real brother and sister.

vocabulary.meaning: to think that ~, to consider ~ to be

grammar: ううん is a casual negative, correcting her own previous 'it felt like' — she upgrades from simile to statement: not 'like siblings' but 'actual siblings.' 〜だと思ってる (te-iru = ongoing state) means 'I currently and continuously think of you as…'

text: ケンかな
translation: Was it Ken?

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder…, was it? (soft self-directed question)

grammar: かな is a sentence-final particle expressing gentle self-directed wondering or uncertainty. This line seems to be a brief interjection — Yuna may be recalling a specific name or memory, pausing to consider.

text: ブリッツをしている若さ
translation: Your youthful energy playing blitzball.
grammar: ブリッツをしている modifies 若さ as a relative clause: 'the youthfulness [that shows] while playing blitzball.' This is a nominal phrase evoking a fond image of Wakka.

text: 好き / おこりんぼのルール
translation: I love it. / Hot-tempered Lulu.

vocabulary.meaning: hothead, someone who gets angry easily (childlike/affectionate term)

grammar: 好き as a standalone statement (no subject or object stated) is elliptical — 'I love [that].' おこりんぼのルール is a fond nickname construction: 'Lulu the hothead,' where おこりんぼ modifies ルール possessively.

text: どんなに叱られても / 好き
translation: No matter how much she scolded me, / I love her.

vocabulary.meaning: no matter how much, however much

grammar: どんなに〜ても is a fixed pattern meaning 'no matter how much ~.' 叱られる is the passive of 叱る ('to be scolded'). The repetition of 好き (love/like) after this concessive clause intensifies the unconditional affection.

text: それから / 新入りガード君
translation: And then… / You, new guardian.

vocabulary.meaning: you (casual, often used for someone younger or familiar)

grammar: 新入りガード君 is a compound address: 新入り ('newcomer') + ガード ('guardian') + 君 (familiar 'you'). Yuna is now turning to address Tidus, calling him affectionately 'you, the new guardian.'

text: 君は
translation: You…
grammar: 君は sets up a topic — 'as for you…' — but the sentence is left incomplete. Yuna is struggling to find the words for what she wants to say about Tidus. The incompleteness communicates more than words could.

text: 君が
translation: You…
grammar: 君が uses が (subject marker) rather than は, signaling that Tidus is the grammatical subject of the coming predicate. But again the sentence breaks off — Yuna switches between frames, struggling to articulate her feelings.

text: えっと
translation: Um…
grammar: えっと is a hesitation filler — equivalent to 'um' or 'well.' It marks a pause in thought, showing that Yuna is genuinely searching for words. The repeated false starts (君は, 君が, えっと, 君と) are emotionally resonant.

text: 君と
translation: With you…
grammar: 君と uses と as the comitative particle ('with you'). Another incomplete fragment — Yuna is cycling through different grammatical framings, each one abandoned before completion, showing the difficulty of expressing her feelings.

text: 会えてよかった / まだ会ってからそんなに経ってないけど
translation: I'm glad I could meet you. / We haven't known each other very long, but…

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to meet (potential of 会う)
I'm glad, it was good (past of よい)
that much, to such a degree

grammar: 会えてよかった: potential te-form + よかった = 'I'm glad I was able to meet [you].' 経ってない is the negative te-iru of 経つ ('time hasn't passed [much]'). けど at the end leaves a contrast hanging.

text: 不思議 / こういうものなのかって思った
translation: It's strange. / I thought — maybe this is just how it is.

vocabulary.meaning: this kind of thing, something like this

grammar: こういうものなのかって思った = 'I thought, is this what this kind of thing is like?' なのか is a soft wondering question embedded within reported thought. The phrase captures an epiphany about connection.

text: それは / 想像してたより / とっても素敵な気持ちで
translation: It was / a much more wonderful feeling than I had imagined,
grammar: 想像してたより = 'more than I had been imagining' — a comparison using より ('than'). 素敵な気持ち is a noun phrase ('a wonderful feeling') and で marks it as a description that connects to the next clause.

text: 素敵だけど
translation: Wonderful, but…
grammar: 素敵だけど sets up a concession: 'it's wonderful, but…' The contrast (beautiful feeling vs. painful consequence) is the emotional core of Yuna's confession to Tidus.

text: 辛いよ
translation: It hurts.
grammar: 辛いよ is direct and raw — a simple い-adjective + よ (assertive). The brevity after a long, roundabout approach makes it land hard. よ conveys a personal, earnest declaration.

text: なんだろう
translation: I wonder why…

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder what it is, why is it? (self-directed puzzlement)

grammar: なんだろう is a self-addressed rhetorical question: 'what is this / why is this?' だろう (conjectural form of だ) combined with なん creates a wondering, reflective tone.

text: うまく言えないや / とにかく会えてよかった
translation: I can't say it well. / Anyway — I'm glad I could meet you.

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to say (potential of 言う)
anyway, at any rate, in any case

grammar: うまく言えないや = 'I can't express it well' — using the negative potential of 言う. や at the end adds a slightly resigned, self-aware softness. とにかく pivots to the bottom line despite the inability to articulate.

text: だから
translation: That's why…
grammar: A repeated だから — building toward the final admission. Each pause and fragment intensifies the emotional weight of what Yuna is trying to say.

text: つらいのかな
translation: Maybe that's why it hurts.

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder if ~ is the case (soft self-questioning)

grammar: 〜のかな = nominalizer の + question か + soft wondering な. The whole phrase is a gentle self-directed question: 'I wonder if [meeting you is why] it hurts.' Yuna is working out her own feelings aloud.

text: 君と
translation: With you…
grammar: Another incomplete fragment — 君と (with you) as a sentence start, left hanging. The recurrence of this phrase across multiple broken fragments emphasizes Yuna's emotional struggle to speak about her feelings for Tidus.

text: 別れるときのことを考えると
translation: When I think about the moment of parting from you,

vocabulary.meaning: to part, to separate, to say goodbye
about the time when ~, the matter of when ~

grammar: 別れるときのことを考えると: 〜と here is the conditional/temporal: 'when/if I think about the time of parting…' The sentence again runs into the next line for its conclusion.

text: 怖いよ
translation: I'm scared.
grammar: The payoff of the previous conditional: 'when I think about parting from you — I'm scared.' 怖いよ mirrors 辛いよ from earlier — the same direct, raw construction. Yuna's fear of losing Tidus is spoken plainly.

text: なんか変だな…ここ…取り直しっす!
translation: This feels strange… here… Let's redo this!

vocabulary.meaning: to redo, to start over, to retake

grammar: 取り直しっす is a youthful/casual speech pattern — 取り直し (noun form of 取り直す: 'redo/retake') + っす (a youth-slang contracted form of です). Tidus suddenly breaks the mood, self-conscious about the recording.

text: えっと…
translation: Um…
grammar: Tidus's second attempt at speaking on the sphere recording starts with えっと — he's nervous and unsure how to begin, mirroring Yuna's earlier hesitation with his own.

text: なーにしてるっすか!
translation: What are you doing?!

vocabulary.meaning: casual question form (contraction of ですか)

grammar: なーに is a drawn-out emphatic form of 何 — surprised or teasing. っすか is a youthful casual question suffix (contraction of ですか). Rikku likely interrupts Tidus's attempt to record, breaking the solemnity with comic energy.

text: 最後かもしれないだろう
translation: This might be the last time, you know.
grammar: This line mirrors the very opening of Chapter 00 — a narrative bookend. だろう adds a seeking quality, as if Tidus is half-convincing himself. The circularity of the line connects the beginning and the end of the story.

text: だから全部話しておきたいんだ
translation: That's why I want to tell you everything.

vocabulary.meaning: to do in advance, to leave done

grammar: This also echoes the game's opening lines exactly. 話しておきたい = 'want to tell [and have it be said/done].' おく adds intentionality — speaking while there is still time. んだ grounds it in personal feeling and explanation.

text: なあ、もっといろいろあったよな / そういえばあの時とか
translation: Hey, there was so much more, wasn't there. / Come to think of it, like that time…

vocabulary.meaning: various things, all sorts of things
come to think of it, now that you mention it

grammar: よな is a casual confirmation-seeking particle combination (よ + な) used among friends: 'there was, wasn't there.' そういえば is a fixed phrase that signals a recalled memory coming to mind. とか adds casualness ('like…' / 'such as…').

text: 誰か、なんかない?
translation: Anyone, got something to add?

vocabulary.meaning: isn't there?, don't you have? (negative question)

grammar: なんかない? is a casual negative question meaning 'don't you have something?' or 'isn't there anything?' Tidus is inviting others around the campfire to share memories before the night ends.

text: あのね / うわ、何? / 思い出話は…もう…おしまい!
translation: You know what— / Wha, what?! / The reminiscing is… over now… Done!
grammar: おしまい is a childlike/emphatic way to declare something over — stronger and more final than 終わり. Rikku interrupts to cut off the emotional atmosphere, her energetic personality breaking the somber mood.

text: 行こう!
translation: Let's go!
grammar: 行こう is the volitional form of 行く, expressing 'let's go!' — an invitation or rallying call. The exclamation mark reinforces the energetic, forward-moving tone as the party enters the dome.

text: 長き旅路を歩む者よ / 名乗りなさい
translation: You who have walked the long road — state your name.

vocabulary.meaning: long (archaic attributive form of 長い)
to give one's name, to introduce oneself

grammar: 長き is an archaic/literary attributive form of 長い, used in formal or ceremonial registers. 〜者よ is a literary vocative: 'O you who are [such a person].' 名乗りなさい is a formal imperative (なさい form), commanding but polite.

text: 召喚師、ユーナです / ビサイドより参りました / 顔を…
translation: I am Yuna, summoner. / I have come from Besaid. / Your face—

vocabulary.meaning: to come, to go (humble form of 来る/行く)

grammar: 参りました is the humble (謙譲語) past tense of 来る — Yuna uses humble speech before this powerful figure. より is a formal particle for 'from' (more formal than から). 顔を… trails off — Yuna begins to recognize the figure's face but is cut off or stops herself.

text: そなたが歩いてきた道を見せなさい
translation: Show me the path you have walked.
grammar: 〜てきた expresses an action that has continued up to the present moment ('the path you have walked'). なさい is a polite imperative form, softer than the plain imperative but still commanding — fitting for Yunalesca's authoritative register.

text: よろしい / 大いに励んだようだな
translation: Good. It seems you have worked hard indeed.

vocabulary.meaning: to strive, to work hard, to exert oneself

grammar: 〜たようだ expresses an inference based on evidence: 'it seems/appears that [you] worked hard.' The な at the end is a sentence-final particle adding a reflective or slightly assertive tone, common in male speech or elevated narration.

text: ユーナレスカ様もそなたを歓迎するであろう
translation: Lady Yunalesca will surely welcome you as well.
grammar: であろう is the formal/literary equivalent of だろう, used here to convey a confident, almost prophetic assertion. The も ('also') implies Yunalesca's welcome echoes the guardian's own approval.

text: ガード州ともども / ユーナレスカ様の身元に向かうがよい
translation: Proceed, together with your guardians, to Lady Yunalesca's presence.

vocabulary.meaning: presence, whereabouts (here used to mean 'before her/in her presence')
to head toward, to proceed to

grammar: 〜がよい is a classical/archaic imperative construction meaning 'you should/it would be good if you…' It conveys an authoritative directive without the bluntness of a plain imperative, befitting a temple guardian's formal speech.

text: スピラを救うためならば / 私の命など喜んで捧げましょう
translation: If it is to save Spira, I would gladly offer up even my life.

vocabulary.meaning: to offer, to dedicate, to sacrifice

grammar: 〜ためならば is a conditional: 'if it is for the sake of…' The など after 命 downplays the speaker's own life ('even a thing like my life'), heightening the self-sacrificial sentiment. 〜ましょう adds a volitional, willing tone.

text: ガードとしてこれほど名誉なことはありません
translation: As a guardian, there is no greater honor than this.
grammar: 〜ほど…はない is a superlative pattern: 'there is nothing as [adjective] as this.' として marks the speaker's role/capacity. The overall structure expresses the highest degree of pride in the sacrificial role.

text: ですからヨン君様 / 必ずやシーンを倒してください
translation: Therefore, Lady Yuna — please, without fail, defeat Sin.
grammar: 必ずや is a more emphatic, literary form of 必ず, conveying an urgent entreaty. The 〜てください is a polite request. This is a past guardian's recorded plea — the echo of someone who has already sacrificed themselves.

text: 何? / 今の何?
translation: What? What was that just now?

vocabulary.meaning: that just now, what just happened

grammar: 今の (literally 'the now one') is a colloquial shorthand for 今のもの or 今のこと — 'the thing just now.' The repeated question fragments reflect a shocked, disbelieving reaction.

text: かつてここを訪れたものだ / ヨン君様に言っていたわね
translation: It was someone who once visited this place. They were speaking to Lady Yuna.
grammar: 〜たものだ can express a habitual past ('used to do') or a reminiscent past action. Here it means 'someone who visited.' The わね at the end is a soft feminine sentence-final particle seeking light confirmation or expressing shared realization.

text: あの人、大将軍師様のガード / 現行中に満ちたこのドームは
translation: That person was a guardian of a great high priest. This dome is filled with memories still in motion.
grammar: The sentence is left incomplete mid-thought, continuing into the next clip. The phrase 現行中に満ちた ('filled with ongoing/living memories') is complex but indicates the dome preserves residual psychic impressions.

text: 巨大なスフィアも同然だ / 思いをとどめています
translation: It is practically a giant sphere. It holds memories within it.

vocabulary.meaning: practically the same as, no different from
to retain, to keep, to preserve

grammar: 〜も同然だ is a useful pattern meaning 'practically the same as, equivalent to.' The dome functions like a giant recording sphere (スフィア) preserving the thoughts and emotions of those who passed through it.

text: いつまでだ
translation: Until when?
grammar: A terse, clipped question — characteristic of Auron's minimalist speech. The implied full question would be 'Until when will it keep holding them?' The bluntness is deliberate, cutting through the exposition.

text: Não é...
translation: (Non-Japanese audio — likely a sound clip or system artifact.)

text: ユーナ、着いたぞ
translation: Yuna, we've arrived.
grammar: The ぞ is a masculine sentence-final particle that adds emphasis and a slightly assertive or alerting tone — 'We're here.' Common in male speech, particularly Auron's direct register.

text: 究極召喚ですね
translation: The Final Summoning, then.
grammar: The ですね at the end is a tag seeking soft confirmation or expressing quiet realization — 'It's the Final Summoning, isn't it.' Yuna's tone here is subdued and resolute, not a question so much as an acknowledgment of what awaits.

text: 行け
translation: Go.
grammar: 行け is the plain imperative (命令形) of 行く. It is maximally terse and commanding — a single syllable order. Auron's signature minimalism: no softening, no explanation, just direction.

text: はぁ? / 究極召喚がねぇだ?
translation: Huh? The Final Summoning is gone?

vocabulary.meaning: huh?, what? (expression of disbelief or confusion)
isn't there, doesn't exist (colloquial negative of ある)

grammar: ねぇ is a dialectal/colloquial contraction of ない, common in Wakka's Besaid dialect. The question particle だ here (rather than か) gives it a blunt, unpolished quality. The はぁ at the start signals genuine shock.

text: アーロンさん!
translation: Auron!
grammar: A simple exclamatory call. Tidus uses さん with Auron, reflecting a respectful but familiar relationship — unlike the more formal 様 used for legendary figures.

text: みんな来て!
translation: Everyone, come here!
grammar: 来て is the te-form of 来る used as an imperative ('come!'). The te-form as a command is slightly softer than the plain imperative 来い but still urgent. みんな addresses the entire group.

text: これ、祈り子様じゃない。ただの石像なの。
translation: This isn't the fayth. It's just a stone statue.

vocabulary.meaning: fayth (one who has been made into a summoning vessel)

grammar: 〜じゃない is a colloquial negative ('it's not'). The なの at the end is a feminine explanatory sentence-final particle — Rikku is explaining what she's observed, with a slightly surprised or informative tone.

text: その像は、すでに祈り子としての力を失っておる。
translation: That statue has already lost its power as a fayth.

vocabulary.meaning: to be (classical/humble auxiliary, here archaic continuative)

grammar: 〜としての marks the capacity or role: 'as a fayth.' 〜ておる is an archaic/dialectal form of 〜ている, used by older or solemn characters to convey gravitas. Yunalesca's speech is consistently formal and archaic.

text: 史上初めて、究極召喚の祈り子となったゼイオン様。
translation: Lord Zaon, who became the very first fayth of the Final Summoning in all of history.

vocabulary.meaning: in history, historically, of all time

grammar: This is a noun phrase (no main verb), functioning as a topic introduction: 'Lord Zaon, who became...' The sentence continues into the next clip. 史上初めて is a set phrase meaning 'for the first time in history.'

text: そのお姿をとどめる像に過ぎる。ゼイオン様はもう、消えてしまわれた。
translation: It is merely a statue preserving his form. Lord Zaon has already faded away.

vocabulary.meaning: to be nothing more than, merely

grammar: 〜に過ぎない (here 〜に過ぎる in continuative) means 'nothing more than.' 消えてしまわれた uses 〜てしまう (completion/regret) + passive honorific られ, indicating Lord Zaon has definitively disappeared — the honorific showing reverence even in describing his loss.

text: 消えた!? / ってことは、究極召喚もなくなっちゃったの!?
translation: He disappeared!? So does that mean the Final Summoning is gone too!?

vocabulary.meaning: so that means, in other words (colloquial)
to cease to exist, to be gone, to disappear
ended up (doing), did completely (colloquial contraction of てしまった)

grammar: ってことは is a colloquial inference marker: 'if that's the case, then…' 〜ちゃったの is 〜てしまったの contracted — expressing surprise and dismay at an irreversible outcome. The の at the end adds a questioning, slightly alarmed tone.

text: ご安心なされ / リオナレスカ様が新たな究極召喚を授けてくださる
translation: Rest assured. Lady Yunalesca will bestow upon you a new Final Summoning.

vocabulary.meaning: please do (archaic/honorific imperative of なさる)
to bestow, to grant, to confer

grammar: ご安心なされ is a formal, archaic way of saying 'please be at ease.' くださる is the honorific form of くれる — 'graciously gives to us' — showing reverence toward Yunalesca. The guardian's speech throughout uses elevated, temple-appropriate language.

text: 召喚師と一心同体に結びつく大いなる力を
translation: A great power that binds to the summoner as one body and soul —

vocabulary.meaning: one heart, one body; completely united
to be bound to, to be connected with

grammar: This is an incomplete sentence (a trailing object phrase), continuing into the next clip. 一心同体 is a four-character compound (四字熟語) meaning absolute unity — one mind, one body. 大いなる is a literary prenominal form of 大いに.

text: 僕に進むがよい / リオナレスカ様の身元へ
translation: You should proceed ahead. To Lady Yunalesca's presence.

vocabulary.meaning: it is good to, you should (archaic volitional directive)
presence, location (used here to mean 'before her')

grammar: 〜がよい is a classical construction used to issue dignified directives ('you would do well to...'). It appears in temple/formal contexts and suits the guardian's ceremonial role.

text: ちょっと待てよ
translation: Hold on a minute.
grammar: 待てよ uses the plain imperative 待て plus よ, which softens the command slightly into an appeal — 'just wait a sec.' This is typical of Tidus's direct, slightly impatient speech style.

text: アーロン / あんた最初から知ってたんだよな
translation: Auron — you knew from the very beginning, didn't you.
grammar: 〜てたんだよな is a casual contracted form of 〜ていたのだよな — a rhetorical tag question demanding confirmation of something the speaker has just realized. The んだ adds an explanatory/revelatory nuance; よな seeks agreement. Tidus is confronting Auron.

text: どうして黙ってたの?
translation: Why did you keep silent?

vocabulary.meaning: to be silent, to stay quiet

grammar: 黙ってたの is 黙っていたの contracted — 'were you silent?' The の at the end is a feminine/neutral soft questioning particle that conveys genuine hurt and confusion rather than anger.

text: お前たち自身に / 真実の姿を見せるためだ
translation: So that you yourselves could see the truth for what it is.
grammar: 〜ためだ expresses purpose: 'it was in order to…' Auron's answer is characteristically elliptical — he answers the 'why' but leaves much unsaid. 真実の姿 (the true form of truth) suggests the party had to witness it themselves to understand.

text: リュウナ
translation: Yuna.

vocabulary.meaning: Yuna (name, possibly a variant pronunciation or mishearing in transcript)

grammar: A simple name-call, likely Kimahri or another guardian addressing Yuna. In moments of gravity, simply saying someone's name carries weight — a check-in, a steadying gesture.

text: もう戻れないよ / 分かっている
translation: There's no going back now. / I know.

vocabulary.meaning: already, no longer (with negative: not anymore)
I know, I understand (already in a state of knowing)

grammar: もう戻れない uses the potential negative (戻れない = cannot return) with もう to indicate the point of no return. 分かっている is the progressive form of 分かる — 'I am already in a state of knowing' — more certain and resolute than 分かった.

text: キマリが先に行く / リュウナの前はキマリが守る
translation: Kimahri will go ahead. Kimahri will protect what lies before Yuna.
grammar: Kimahri refers to himself in the third person throughout the game — a distinctive speech trait. リュウナの前 (what lies before Yuna) frames his protection as guarding her path forward. The structure is simple and declarative, matching Kimahri's terseness.

text: なんか出てくるよ!
translation: Something's coming out!
grammar: なんか is a casual contraction of 何か. 出てくる uses 〜てくる to indicate movement toward the speaker. The よ at the end is an assertive particle alerting others to something the speaker has noticed.

text: ようこそザナルカンドへ / 長い旅路を越え
translation: Welcome to Zanarkand. Having crossed a long journey —
grammar: The sentence is suspended after 越え (the conjunctive/te-form of 越える), flowing into the next line. 旅路 is a more poetic word for journey than 旅 alone. Yunalesca's opening speech is ceremonial and measured.

text: よくぞたどり着きました
translation: You have done well to arrive here at last.

vocabulary.meaning: how well you have, truly (emphatic praise, literary)
to finally reach, to arrive after great effort

grammar: よくぞ is a classical emphatic adverb expressing admiration — 'you have truly done well to…' It elevates the verb it modifies. たどり着く implies arrival after struggle or long effort, unlike simply 着く. The combination is solemn and ceremonious.

text: 大いなる祝福を / 今こそ授けましょう
translation: Now is the moment — I shall bestow upon you a great blessing.

vocabulary.meaning: now of all times, now is the moment

grammar: 今こそ is an emphatic temporal expression — 'now, at this very moment.' The こそ adds contrastive/emphatic focus. 〜ましょう is a volitional/offering form: 'I will/let me bestow.' Yunalesca frames the Final Summoning as a gift, masking its horror.

text: 我が究極の秘技
translation: My ultimate secret art —
grammar: A suspended noun phrase — 'my ultimate secret technique' — no verb, left hanging dramatically before the next line completes the thought. 我が is archaic possessive, lending Yunalesca an ancient, other-worldly quality.

text: 究極召喚を
translation: The Final Summoning —

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

grammar: を marks the object of the implied verb from the previous/next clause. Another dramatic pause — Yunalesca names the summoning itself before describing how it works, building suspense.

text: 選ぶのです / あ、え? / あなたが選んだ勇士を人
translation: You must choose. / Huh, what? / The brave one whom you have chosen —
grammar: 〜のです (or んです) provides an explanatory or assertive nuance — 'It is that you must choose.' The interjections あ、え? indicate surprise from a party member reacting to Yunalesca's words. The trailing 人 may be a speech fragment or transcription quirk.

text: 私の力で変えましょう
translation: I will transform them with my power.
grammar: 〜ましょう here is volitional/offering: 'I shall/I will.' The phrase continues from the previous clip: Yunalesca explains she will transform the chosen guardian into the Final Aeon — euphemistically framing the sacrificial process as a 'transformation.'

text: あなたの究極召喚の祈りごり
translation: The fayth of your Final Summoning —

vocabulary.meaning: fayth (one who becomes the vessel of a summoning)

grammar: The text appears to be a slightly distorted transcription of 祈り子 (いのりご). Another suspended object phrase leading into the next clause. Yunalesca is slowly, methodically explaining the process of the Final Summoning — each fragment building the full picture.

text: 思いの力 絆の力
translation: The power of feelings. The power of bonds.
grammar: Two parallel noun phrases with no explicit verb — Yunalesca is enumerating the source of the Final Summoning's power. The parallelism (思いの力 / 絆の力) gives the speech a hymn-like, ceremonial rhythm.

text: その結晶こそ究極召喚 / 召喚師と強く結ばれたものが
translation: That crystallization is none other than the Final Summoning. The one who is deeply bonded with the summoner —

vocabulary.meaning: crystal, crystallization; the distilled essence of something
to be bound, to be connected (passive)

grammar: こそ is an emphatic focus particle: 'that crystallization is precisely / is indeed the Final Summoning.' It emphasizes that the summoning is not just a technique but the literal crystallization of bonds. The second clause trails into the next segment.

text: 祈り子となって得られる力
translation: The power that can be gained by becoming the fayth.
grammar: 〜となって links becoming the fayth to gaining the power — 'by becoming the fayth, [one] can obtain [this] power.' 得られる is the potential passive: 'can be obtained.' The sentence completes the thought from clip_123.

text: 二人を結ぶ思いの絆が / 真を倒す光となります
translation: The bond of feelings that connects the two will become the light that defeats Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: to connect, to tie, to bind

grammar: A beautiful but dark sentence: the bond between summoner and guardian becomes the weapon against Sin — but only through the guardian's death. 〜となります is the polite form of になる, 'to become.' The 真 here likely means シン (Sin) — a transcription issue.

text: 千年前
translation: A thousand years ago —
grammar: A time phrase fragment left suspended — 'A thousand years ago,' — serving as a dramatic time marker before Yunalesca recounts her own history. The brevity creates a pause, a weight of millennia behind her words.

text: 私は我が夫 ゼイオンを選びました
translation: I chose my husband, Zaon.
grammar: A devastating revelation delivered with quiet formality. 我が夫 uses the archaic possessive — Yunalesca is 1000 years old and speaks as someone from another era. She sacrificed her own husband to defeat Sin the first time.

text: ゼイオンを祈り後に変え / 私の究極召喚を得たのです
translation: I transformed Zaon into the fayth and obtained my Final Summoning.
grammar: 〜に変え is the conjunctive of 〜に変える, linking 'transforming into fayth' with 'obtaining the summoning.' 〜たのです adds an explanatory finality, as if Yunalesca is making the record clear — this is what was done, this is how it works.

text: 恐れることはありません / あなたの悲しみはすべて解き放たれるでしょう
translation: There is nothing to fear. All of your sadness will be set free.
grammar: 恐れることはありません: 'There is no thing to fear' — ことはない is a pattern meaning 'there is no need/reason to.' 〜でしょう is a soft prediction/conjecture: 'will probably/surely be.' Yunalesca casts death as liberation from sorrow — a seductive but sinister framing.

text: 究極召喚を発動すれば / あなたの命も散るのです
translation: When you unleash the Final Summoning, your life too will be scattered.

vocabulary.meaning: to activate, to unleash, to invoke
to scatter, to disperse, to fall (like petals); to die

grammar: 〜すれば is a conditional: 'if/when you activate it.' 散る carries poetic resonance in Japanese — the scattering of petals as a metaphor for death. のです adds an explanatory, matter-of-fact gravity. Yunalesca states the summoner's death as simply part of the process.

text: 命が消えるその時に / 悲しみは消え去ります
translation: At the moment your life fades, your sorrow will vanish entirely.

vocabulary.meaning: to disappear, to fade, to vanish
at that moment, at that time
to completely vanish, to disappear entirely

grammar: 消え去る (消える + 去る) is a compound that emphasizes complete, irreversible disappearance — stronger than 消える alone. The parallel structure (命が消える / 悲しみは消え去る) creates a poetic equation: death = the end of sorrow. Yunalesca uses beauty to sell annihilation.

text: あなたの父
translation: Your father —
grammar: A suspended phrase — 'your father' — creating a dramatic pause before the revelation. Yunalesca is about to draw the direct line between Yuna and Braska's fate.

text: ブラスカもまた同じ道を選びました
translation: Braska, too, chose the same path.
grammar: もまた stacks both も and また for emphasis: 'also and likewise.' 道を選ぶ ('to choose a path') is a common metaphor for a life decision. Here it means Braska chose to complete the pilgrimage knowing he would die — and so did his guardian, Jecht.

text: 俺なりに考えたんだ / それによアロン
translation: I thought it over in my own way. Right, Auron?

vocabulary.meaning: in one's own way, according to one's own manner
right?, isn't that so? (seeking agreement, colloquial)

grammar: 〜なりに means 'in [one's] own way' — acknowledging limitations while asserting personal thought. んだ gives an explanatory/revelatory tone: 'the thing is, I thought about it.' それによ is a colloquial tag seeking confirmation — Jecht's rough, casual register.

text: 無限の可能性なんて信じるとしてもねえんだ俺は
translation: As for me, I don't really believe in things like 'infinite possibilities.'

vocabulary.meaning: things like, such a thing as (dismissive/downplaying)

grammar: なんて dismissively quotes or references 'infinite possibilities,' treating the concept as something he doesn't quite buy into. としても means 'even if [I were to believe],' — he's acknowledging the concept but distancing himself from it. ねえんだ is colloquial for ないんだ — 'I just don't have [that belief].' 俺は at the end is topically emphatic: 'as for me.'

text: ジェクト / なんだ
translation: Jecht. / What?
grammar: A brief exchange — Auron calls Jecht's name; Jecht responds with the casual なんだ. The bluntness of なんだ (rather than はい or 何ですか) is pure Jecht: gruff, direct, never deferential even in solemn moments.

text: 止めても無駄だぞ / すまん
translation: It's useless trying to stop me. / …Sorry.

vocabulary.meaning: sorry, forgive me (rough masculine form of すまない)

grammar: 〜ても無駄だ: 'Even if [you] do X, it's useless' — a dismissal of any attempt to interfere. ぞ adds masculine assertiveness. すまん is the rough form of すみません — Jecht's apology is gruff and brief, but in context (about to become the fayth/Sin), it carries enormous weight.

text: ありがとう / ブラスカにはまだシンを倒すって大仕事が待ってる
translation: Thank you. Braska still has a big job waiting for him — defeating Sin.
grammar: 〜って is a colloquial quotation/description marker: 'the big job of defeating Sin.' The 〜が待ってる (waiting) frames Braska's mission as something still ahead that must be accomplished — Jecht is making sure the focus stays on Braska, not on his own sacrifice.

text: 俺の分までブラスカを守れよ
translation: Guard Braska for my share too.
grammar: 俺の分まで: 'up to and including my share' — he's telling Auron to pick up the slack for both of them. 守れよ is the plain imperative of 守る plus the pleading/soft-assertive よ — not a harsh command but a heartfelt request. One of Jecht's most emotionally revealing moments.

text: まあ、アーロンの言うことも最もだ
translation: Well, what Auron says is reasonable too.

vocabulary.meaning: well, I suppose, in any case
most, extremely; reasonable, logical (also written 尤も)

grammar: 最もだ here means 'it's reasonable/valid' (尤もだ). まあ softens the concession — Jecht isn't fully agreeing, just acknowledging the point. This is a moment where Jecht is reluctantly accepting the logic of the situation.

text: よし、俺が何とかしてやる
translation: Alright, I'll figure something out.

vocabulary.meaning: to manage somehow, to work something out

grammar: よし is a self-motivating exclamation marking a decision. 〜てやる is an assertive/determined volitional form, often implying doing something for others: 'I'll do it [for you/them].' This is very Jecht — brash resolve in the face of an impossible situation.

text: 何か策があるというのか?
translation: You're saying you have some plan?

vocabulary.meaning: are you saying that, do you mean (skeptical/questioning)

grammar: 〜というのか is a skeptical interrogative: 'Are you actually saying that you have a plan?' It expresses doubt that the preceding claim is credible. Auron's pragmatic skepticism of Jecht's bravado is perfectly encapsulated here.

text: ジェクト / 無限の可能性にでも期待すっか
translation: Jecht. / Maybe I'll just pin my hopes on 'infinite possibilities' or whatever.

vocabulary.meaning: to expect, to hope, to pin hopes on

grammar: にでも marks a casual, somewhat self-deprecating selection: 'on something like infinite possibilities, I guess.' すっか is a very casual volitional tag — 'I might as well, huh?' Jecht is referencing Auron's earlier phrase while mocking his own hopelessness, half-laughing at the absurdity of his situation.

text: そして、何も変わらなかった
translation: And yet, nothing changed.
grammar: A simple, devastating statement — Auron's narration of history: despite Braska and Jecht's sacrifice, Sin returned and nothing fundamentally changed. The past tense 変わらなかった makes it absolute. そして at the start creates a narrative pivot, linking past action to its futile result.

text: 俺たちが変えてやる / どうやって?
translation: We'll change it. / How?
grammar: 〜てやる expresses strong, slightly defiant determination: 'we'll change it [ourselves]!' It often implies doing something for someone or in spite of opposition. どうやって? is a blunt practical question — acknowledging the determination but demanding a real plan.

text: 作戦なんて何もねえんだろ
translation: You don't have any plan at all, do you.

vocabulary.meaning: there isn't, right? (colloquial negative + rhetorical tag)

grammar: なんて after 作戦 dismisses the very concept that a plan exists. ねえんだろ (ないんだろ) is a rhetorical tag confirming the speaker's assumption — 'there's no plan, right?' Wakka is being realistic, not cruel, but it stings.

text: 誰かが祈り子になる必要があるのに / 私、いいよ
translation: Someone needs to become the fayth, even so — I'll do it.

vocabulary.meaning: there is a need, it is necessary
even though, despite the fact that (conjunctive with nuance of regret or complaint)

grammar: のに here creates a tension between the necessity and the unspoken wish that it weren't so — 'even though someone needs to, [and that's unfortunate]…' いいよ is understated self-sacrifice: 'I'll do it, it's fine.' Yuna's characteristic quiet courage — she minimizes her own sacrifice.

text: 俺もだ、ユナ
translation: Me too, Yuna.
grammar: 俺もだ is a direct and blunt way of saying 'me too' or 'same for me' — also willing to be the fayth. This moment reveals multiple party members willing to sacrifice themselves, which is both moving and the crisis Tidus pushes back against.

text: それじゃあ、親父たちと一緒だろ / 凪雪救って、そんだけだ
translation: Then that's the same as our fathers, isn't it. Save Spira, that's it — that's all.

vocabulary.meaning: our fathers, the old men (colloquial plural)
just that, that's all (colloquial contraction of それだけ)

grammar: Tidus is calling out the contradiction — accepting the fayth sacrifice would just repeat Braska and Jecht's cycle. 凪雪 appears to be a transcription error for スピラ (Spira). そんだけ is very colloquial and dismissive — 'that's all it amounts to.' Tidus refuses to accept a 'save the world and die' ending.

text: また復活しちゃうだろ / あのな、シンを倒してユーナも死なせねえ / そんでシンの復活も止めたいってか?
translation: And Sin will just revive again, right? Look, you want to defeat Sin without letting Yuna die — and also stop Sin from coming back?

vocabulary.meaning: to revive, to come back to life
to let die, to cause to die (causative)
is that what you mean?, you're saying that? (colloquial rhetorical)

grammar: 復活しちゃうだろ: 'it'll come back, right?' — ちゃう is the colloquial contraction of てしまう (unwanted outcome). 死なせねえ is colloquial negative causative: 'won't let [her] die.' The whole line is Wakka summarizing Tidus's impossible goal back to him, somewhat incredulously.

text: 全部叶えば最高だけどよ / 欲張りすぎたら、全部失敗するわ
translation: It would be great if all of that could come true, but — if you're too greedy, you'll fail at everything.

vocabulary.meaning: to come true, to be realized, to be fulfilled

grammar: 〜ば最高だけど: 'it would be great if [that happened], but…' — a conditional expressing a wishful scenario with a realistic counter. 欲張りすぎる: 'to be too greedy' (すぎる = too much). 〜したら introduces a conditional leading to the consequence of total failure. Wakka is the pragmatist here.

text: 嫌だ、欲張れ / 青臭いこと言うなよ
translation: No, be greedy! / Don't say such naive things.

vocabulary.meaning: no, I don't want that, I refuse
to be greedy, to want more than one's share

grammar: 欲張れ is the plain imperative — 'be greedy!' Tidus is reclaiming the word as a positive. 青臭いこと言うなよ: 〜な (prohibitive imperative) + よ = 'don't say [those] naive things.' Tidus pushes back on Wakka's pragmatism, defending idealism.

text: 青くてもいい!大人ぶってカッコつけてさ / 言いたいことも言えないなんて絶対嫌だ! そんなんじゃ何も変えられない!
translation: Being naive is fine! Pretending to be an adult and acting cool — not being able to say what you want to say, I absolutely hate that! You can't change anything that way!

vocabulary.meaning: to act grown-up, to pretend to be mature
to act cool, to show off, to strike a pose

grammar: 青くてもいい uses the te-form of an い-adjective + もいい: 'even if [I'm] naive, that's fine.' 大人ぶって and カッコつけて are in te-form, listing behaviors Tidus rejects. 言いたいことも言えないなんて絶対嫌だ: 〜なんて + 嫌だ is a strong rejection of a situation. This is one of Tidus's key character speeches — refusing to suppress emotion for the sake of appearing cool or adult.

text: 俺、この青さはなくさない。 / ああ、どうしたらいいかなんてわかんないよ。
translation: I won't lose this naivety of mine. Yeah, I have no idea what the right thing to do is.

vocabulary.meaning: naivety, greenness, immaturity (the noun form of 青い/青臭い)
to lose, to get rid of
don't understand, have no idea (colloquial negative)

grammar: なくさない is the volitional negative — a firm decision not to lose something. 青さ nominalizes the adjective 青い (naive/green) — Tidus is owning his naivety as a defining quality. どうしたらいいかなんてわかんない: 'I have no idea what to do' — using なんて to slightly distance the question from himself, honestly admitting uncertainty.

text: でも、10年前のアーロンが言ってたこと、俺も信じるす。
translation: But I also believe what Auron said ten years ago.
grammar: A touching callback — Tidus references words Auron said to Jecht (about 'infinite possibilities') ten years before the game's events. 言ってたこと: 'the thing [he] was saying' — 〜ていた contracted. 俺も信じるす appears to be a slightly garbled transcription of 俺も信じる — 'I also believe it.'

text: 無限の可能性?
translation: Infinite possibilities?
grammar: A one-line echo — Auron or another party member repeating the phrase back. The question mark suggests surprise or wry acknowledgment. The phrase 無限の可能性 has become a thematic throughline connecting Jecht, Auron, and now Tidus.

text: うん。俺、行ってくる。ユーナレスカに話聞く。
translation: Yeah. I'm going. I'll hear what Yunalesca has to say.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm going (and will come back); set off and return
to listen to what someone has to say, to hear someone out

grammar: 行ってくる is the standard Japanese phrase for 'I'm heading out' — literally 'I'll go and come back,' implying a return. It's casual and decisive. Tidus's plan is simple: go talk to Yunalesca and find another way. The simplicity of the phrasing contrasts with the enormity of what he's about to do.

text: 聞いたら、なんとかなるのかな?
translation: If I talk to her, do you think something will work out?

vocabulary.meaning: to work out somehow, to manage
I wonder…; expresses mild uncertainty or hope

grammar: 〜たら is a conditional ('if/when I ask'). なんとかなるのかな combines なんとかなる (things will work out) + の (nominalizer/soft emphasis) + かな (wondering). The whole phrase is a hopeful, uncertain question to oneself.

text: サナ、わかんないけど
translation: I don't know, but…

vocabulary.meaning: don't know (colloquial contraction of わからない)

grammar: わかんない is casual speech for わからない. The sentence trails off with けど, leaving the rest implied — a common pattern in Japanese for softening a statement or leaving space for the listener to fill in.

text: 俺の物語、くだらない物語だったら
translation: If my story turns out to be a worthless story…
grammar: 〜だったら is a past-tense conditional ('if it were/turns out to be'). The sentence is left incomplete — the conclusion is stated in the next line. This fragmented speech style conveys emotional build-up.

text: ここで終わらせてやる! / 待って!
translation: I'll end it right here! / Wait!

vocabulary.meaning: to bring to an end, to finish (causative of 終わる)
to do something (with strong, defiant resolve; rough masculine speech)

grammar: 〜てやる carries a forceful, defiant nuance — 'I'll damn well do it.' It is rougher than 〜てあげる. The juxtaposition with 待って from another speaker creates a dramatic back-and-forth.

text: 私にとっては、私の物語なんだよ
translation: For me, it's my story too, you know.

vocabulary.meaning: it is (emphatic; seeking understanding or asserting)

grammar: 〜にとっては marks perspective ('for me'). なんだよ = なのだよ, a soft but firm assertion. Yuna is telling Tidus that his story is hers too — she has a stake in it.

text: 振り回されてちゃダメ / ゆらゆら揺れて流されちゃダメ / どんな結末だってきっと後悔する
translation: I can't be tossed around. / I can't drift and be swept away. / Whatever the ending, I'll surely have regrets.

vocabulary.meaning: to swing around; to jerk around, to be controlled by others
to be swept away, to go along with the flow

grammar: 〜てちゃダメ = 〜てしまっては+ダメ, 'it's no good if I end up doing X.' どんな〜だって means 'no matter what kind of ~.' きっと adds certainty ('surely').

text: そんなのも… / 嫌だ
translation: That too… / I don't want that.

vocabulary.meaning: something like that, that kind of thing (colloquial)
I don't want it, I hate it, no

grammar: そんなの is a casual pronoun ('that sort of thing'). The ellipsis before 嫌だ shows hesitation and emotional weight. 嫌だ is a raw, childlike declaration of refusal — Yuna asserting her will.

text: 私… / 決める
translation: I… / I'll decide.
grammar: The pause between 私 and 決める is dramatically significant — subject stated alone, then the verb, for emphasis. Present-tense 決める used as a volitional declaration ('I will decide').

text: 自分で決める
translation: I'll decide for myself.
grammar: 自分で adds the nuance of personal agency — 'I, myself, will decide' rather than being decided for. This is Yuna's pivotal declaration of self-determination, breaking from the fate imposed on her.

text: その前に教えてください / 究極召喚で倒してもシンは絶対に蘇るのでしょうか
translation: Before that, please tell me — even if we defeat Sin with the Final Summoning, will Sin absolutely be revived?

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

vocabulary.meaning: to be revived, to come back to life

grammar: 〜てもシンは絶対に蘇るのでしょうか is a polite question pattern: 〜ても ('even if') + のでしょうか (seeking confirmation politely). Yuna is confronting Yunalesca directly with the truth she already suspects.

text: シンは不滅です / シンを倒した究極召喚獣が新たなシンとなり変わり
translation: Sin is immortal. / The Final Aeon that defeats Sin transforms into the new Sin.

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかんじゅう

vocabulary.meaning: to transform into, to change and become

grammar: 不滅です is a declarative statement. The second clause uses the pattern 〜となり変わり — the V-stem of 変わる connected by て/i-form continuation, indicating transformation.

text: 必ずや復活を遂げます / そんで親父がシンかよ
translation: It will surely be revived. / So that means Dad became Sin?

vocabulary.meaning: to accomplish, to achieve, to complete

grammar: 必ずや is a formal emphatic adverb ('without fail'). そんで is casual for それで ('so then'). 〜かよ is a rough masculine particle expressing shocked disbelief — Tidus processing that his father Jecht became Sin.

text: シンはスピラが背負った運を / 永遠に変えられぬ宿命です
translation: Sin is the fate that Spira bears — a destiny that can never be changed.

vocabulary.meaning: to carry on one's back, to bear (a burden)

grammar: 背負った is a modifying relative clause ('the fate that Spira carries'). 変えられぬ is the classical negative potential form of 変えられる — equivalent to 変えられない in modern Japanese, but more formal and absolute in tone.

text: 永遠にって
translation: Forever…?

vocabulary.meaning: quotation/echo particle — repeating what was just said in disbelief

grammar: って here is an echo particle — the speaker repeats a word just heard to express surprise, disbelief, or the need to process it. It is a very natural Japanese reaction pattern.

text: でもよ / 人間が罪を全部償えば / シンの復活は止まるんだろ
translation: But, you know — if humanity atones for all its sins, Sin's revival will stop, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to atone for, to make amends

grammar: でもよ is a colloquial opener ('but hey'). 〜えば is a conditional ('if we atone'). 〜んだろ = のだろう, seeking confirmation with a rough masculine tone ('that's how it works, right?').

text: いつかはきっと何とかなんだろう
translation: Someday it'll surely work out somehow, right?

vocabulary.meaning: someday (with the nuance of 'eventually, at some point')

grammar: いつかは adds emphasis to someday ('there will come a time'). きっと reinforces certainty. This is Tidus clinging to the Yevonite teaching — the hopeful but naive faith that atonement will eventually end Sin.

text: 人の罪が消えることなど / ありますか
translation: Can human sin ever truly disappear?

vocabulary.meaning: such a thing as (dismissive or rhetorical nuance)

grammar: 〜ことなどありますか is a rhetorical question: 'Does such a thing as X even exist?' The use of など adds a dismissive nuance — 'something like that.' Yunalesca's point: human sin can never disappear, so Sin will never stop.

text: 答えになっています
translation: That is itself the answer.

vocabulary.meaning: has become, serves as (state of being)

grammar: 〜になっています indicates a current state that has been established ('it has become / it serves as'). Yunalesca means her rhetorical question was itself the answer — a cold, circular logic.

text: 罪が消えればシンも消える / エボンはそう教えてきたのです
translation: If sin disappears, so will Sin — that is what Yevon has taught.

vocabulary.meaning: has been doing (up to now) — progressive continuation toward present

grammar: 〜てきたのです combines 〜てきた (an action continued up to the present) + のです (explanatory emphasis). Yunalesca is explaining that this has been Yevon's teaching all along — presented now as cold, cynical manipulation.

text: その教えだけがスピラの希望だった
translation: That teaching alone was Spira's hope.
grammar: だけ limits ('only that teaching'). The past tense だった is notable — Yunalesca speaks of hope in the past tense, as if she knows it is already being dismantled by this conversation.

text: 希望は慰め悲しい運命も諦めて
translation: Hope is a comfort — it gives people the strength to accept even a sad fate.

vocabulary.meaning: to give up, to accept (one's fate)

grammar: 慰め here is used as a predicate noun ('hope is comfort'). 〜も諦めて continues to the next line — the て-form links the idea: hope comforts people and lets them accept even sad fates.

text: 受け入れるための力となる / ふざけるな
translation: …it becomes the power to accept fate. / Don't be ridiculous!

vocabulary.meaning: for the purpose of, in order to
don't joke around, stop it, are you serious?! (angry)

grammar: 〜ための力 = 'power for the purpose of accepting.' となる = 'to become.' ふざけるな is a blunt prohibitive form (dictionary form + な) — a furious rejection. Auron or Tidus cuts off Yunalesca's justification.

text: ただの気休めではないか
translation: Isn't it nothing but empty comfort?

vocabulary.meaning: empty comfort, palliative, something that only makes you feel better temporarily

grammar: ただの dismisses something as trivial. 気休め is a compound: 気 (spirit/feeling) + 休め (rest) — the feeling of rest without real remedy. ではないか is a challenging rhetorical question.

text: ブラスカは教えを信じて命を捨てた / ジェクトはブラスカを信じて犠牲になった
translation: Braska believed in the teachings and gave his life. / Jecht believed in Braska and became the sacrifice.

vocabulary.meaning: to throw away one's life, to die willingly

grammar: Two parallel structures using 〜を信じて (believing in X) + the result. 〜て here is the connective て-form showing cause and result. Auron lays out the painful truth: both men died for a lie.

text: 究極召喚とエボンの教えは
translation: The Final Summoning and Yevon's teachings —

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

grammar: The sentence is left hanging with は (topic marker), with the predicate delivered in the next line. This split across clips creates dramatic pacing.

text: スピラを照らす希望の光
translation: …the light of hope that illuminates Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: to illuminate, to shine light on

grammar: 照らす modifies 希望の光 as a relative clause ('the light of hope that illuminates Spira'). This is the predicate completing the sentence begun in the previous line — Yunalesca's grandiose self-justification.

text: 希望を否定するのなら
translation: If you are going to deny that hope —

vocabulary.meaning: if (that is the case); conditional with emphasis on the stated premise

grammar: 〜のなら is a conditional that acknowledges the premise as already established ('given that you are going to deny it'). The sentence is incomplete — the consequence follows in the next line.

text: 生きても悲しいだけでしょう
translation: …even if you live, there will only be sadness.
grammar: 〜ても means 'even if.' だけでしょう = 'it'll be nothing but.' Yunalesca uses polite でしょう, which is almost condescending here — a cold, composed assertion that life without her hope is meaningless.

text: さあ選ぶのです
translation: Now, choose.
grammar: 〜のです (or のだ) here functions as a command with explanatory force: 'this is the thing you must do.' さあ adds urgency. It is softer in form than the imperative but just as firm in meaning.

text: あなたの祈り子は誰 / 希望のために捧げる犠牲を
translation: Who will be your fayth? / Name the sacrifice you will offer for hope.

vocabulary.meaning: fayth (the being who becomes the core of a summoning)
to offer, to dedicate, to sacrifice

grammar: 誰 is a bare question ('who?'). 捧げる犠牲を — the を object trails without a verb, a dramatic ellipsis demanding an answer. Yunalesca presses Yuna to name who among her guardians will die.

text: 嫌です
translation: No. I refuse.

vocabulary.meaning: I don't want to, I refuse (polite)

grammar: 嫌です is the polite form of 嫌だ. Simple, short, and absolute. The contrast between the politeness of the form and the absoluteness of the refusal is very powerful — Yuna's quiet, firm rejection.

text: 死んでもいいと思ってました / 私の命が役に立つなら
translation: I thought it would be all right to die — if my life could be of use.

vocabulary.meaning: to be useful, to serve a purpose

grammar: 〜てもいい expresses permission or acceptability ('it's okay to die'). 思ってました is past progressive — she had been thinking this for a long time. なら is a conditional based on a premise already in place.

text: 死ぬのも怖くないって
translation: I told myself I wasn't even afraid of dying.

vocabulary.meaning: quotation particle — quoting one's own thoughts

grammar: 〜のも怖くない: のも makes 'dying' a topic ('as for dying, too'), 怖くない = not afraid. って quotes an internal thought or belief Yuna held — 'I kept telling myself that.'

text: 究極召喚は / 何一つ変えられないまやかしなのですね
translation: The Final Summoning — it's an illusion that changes absolutely nothing, isn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: not a single thing, nothing at all

grammar: 何一つ is a strong negative intensifier ('not even one thing'). まやかし is a noun meaning deception/illusion. 〜なのですね combines the explanatory のです with the soft confirmation ね — Yuna states her realization sadly rather than accusatorially.

text: いいえ / 希望の光です
translation: No. It is the light of hope.
grammar: Simple, declarative refusal. Yunalesca does not engage with Yuna's argument — she simply reiterates her doctrine. The bluntness reveals the hollowness of her 'hope.'

text: あなたの父も希望のため犠牲となりました / 悲しみを忘れるために
translation: Your father too became a sacrifice for hope — in order to forget sorrow.
grammar: 〜のために ('for the purpose of'). 悲しみを忘れるために continues with an infinitive purpose clause. Yunalesca co-opts Braska's sacrifice for her own framework — Tidus will sharply rebut this.

text: 違う父さんは
translation: No — my father —

vocabulary.meaning: to be different, to be wrong; 'No, that's not right'

grammar: 違う as a standalone exclamation means 'that's wrong / no.' 父さんは cuts off — the は marks the topic but the sentence is left incomplete in this clip, continuing in the next.

text: 父さんの願いは悲しみを消すことだった
translation: My father's wish was to erase sorrow.
grammar: 〜ことだった nominalizes the verb ('the thing of erasing') and makes it the predicate. Tidus corrects Yunalesca: Braska didn't want to make people forget sorrow — he wanted to eliminate it entirely, a crucial distinction.

text: 忘れたりごまかすことじゃない / 消せない悲しみに逆らって
translation: Not forgetting it or glossing over it — fighting against a sorrow that can't be erased.

vocabulary.meaning: to gloss over, to deceive, to cover up
to go against, to resist, to defy

grammar: 〜たりごまかすことじゃない: the pattern 〜たり〜したりcombined with こと ('doing things like forgetting or glossing over'). じゃない negates it. 消せない is a potential negative modifying 悲しみ ('sorrow that cannot be erased').

text: 何の意味があるのです
translation: What meaning could that possibly have?

vocabulary.meaning: what kind of, any (often rhetorical: 'what possible ~')

grammar: 何の〜があるのですか is a rhetorical question dismissing the idea entirely. Yunalesca counters Tidus: if sorrow can't be erased, what's the point of fighting it? Her logic is that only forgetting (through death/the Final Summoning) brings real peace.

text: 父さんのこと大好きだった
translation: I loved my father so much.

vocabulary.meaning: to love dearly, to like very much

grammar: 〜のこと is a pattern for talking about a person as a topic ('about/regarding father'). 大好きだった is the simple past — now that Braska is gone, Tidus uses past tense. This is Yuna's deeply personal emotional grounding for what follows.

text: だから父さんにできなかったこと私の手で叶えたい
translation: That's why I want to accomplish with my own hands what my father couldn't.

vocabulary.meaning: couldn't do, was unable to accomplish
with one's hands, by one's own effort
to make come true, to fulfill (a wish)

grammar: 父さんにできなかったこと is a relative clause modifying an implied object ('the thing father couldn't do'). 私の手で emphasizes personal agency. 〜たい expresses desire. Yuna's mission is defined by love, not doctrine.

text: 悲しくても生きます / 生きて戦っていつか
translation: Even if it's sorrowful, I will live. / I'll live and fight, and someday —
grammar: 〜ても is concessive ('even if'). 生きます is a volitional declaration in polite form. 生きて戦って — the て-form chains two verbs ('live and fight'). いつか trails off, with the conclusion in the next line.

text: 今は変えられない運命でもいつか / 必ず変える
translation: Even a fate that can't be changed now — someday, I will definitely change it.
grammar: 今は〜でもいつか: 'even if it's X now, someday.' 必ず adds absolute resolve. 変える is the plain volitional form — a promise made to herself and the world. This is Yuna's central vow.

text: まやかしの希望なんかいらない
translation: I don't need a fake hope.

vocabulary.meaning: such a thing as, something like (dismissive)

grammar: なんか here is a dismissive particle attached to a noun ('something like fake hope'). いらない is a direct rejection. Short, blunt, and total — Yuna refuses Yunalesca's entire framework.

text: 哀れなの、自ら希望を捨てるとは
translation: How pitiful — to willingly throw away hope.

vocabulary.meaning: the fact that (exclamatory, often expressing disbelief or emotion)

grammar: 哀れなの is an exclamation of pity (の here is feminine sentence-final). 自ら〜とは is an exclamatory pattern expressing amazement or contempt: 'to think that you yourselves would abandon hope…!'

text: ならば、あなたが絶望に沈む前に
translation: Then, before you sink into despair —

vocabulary.meaning: if that is so, then (formal conditional)

grammar: ならば is a more formal/literary conditional than なら. 〜前に means 'before ~.' The sentence is incomplete — Yunalesca's threat continues in the next line. The imagery of 'sinking into despair' is vivid.

text: せめてもの救いを与えましょう / 悲しい闇に生きるより、希望の光に満ちた死を
translation: Let me at least give you salvation — rather than living in sad darkness, a death filled with the light of hope.

vocabulary.meaning: at least (as small a consolation as possible)

grammar: せめても is 'at the very least.' 〜より sets up a comparison ('rather than living in darkness'). The final noun 死を (death, as object) trails without a verb — a chilling ellipsis. Yunalesca frames killing them as mercy.

text: すべての悲しみを忘れるのです
translation: Forget all your sorrow.
grammar: 〜のです as a command: 'you must forget.' The gentle surface form of のです is eerie here — Yunalesca speaks of killing them as if doing them a kindness, her tone calm and benevolent even as she attacks.

text: さあ、どうする? / 今こそ決断する時だ
translation: So, what are you going to do? / Now is the time to make your decision.

vocabulary.meaning: what will you do, what do you intend to do
now is exactly the time, this is the moment

grammar: 今こそ uses こそ for emphasis ('now, of all times'). 〜する時だ = 'it is the time to ~.' This could be Auron speaking to Tidus, rallying the party to fight Yunalesca.

text: 死んで楽になるか / 生きて悲しみと戦うか
translation: Die and find ease — or live and fight against sorrow?

vocabulary.meaning: to become comfortable, to find relief

grammar: Two parallel 〜か clauses presenting a binary choice. 〜て connects verb + result ('die and thereby become comfortable'). This is the thematic crux of the scene articulated as a direct question.

text: 自分の心で感じたままに / 物語を動かす時だ
translation: Follow exactly what your heart feels — it's time to move the story forward.

vocabulary.meaning: just as, following (a state or feeling)

vocabulary.reading: ものがたりをうごかす
vocabulary.meaning: to move the story, to advance the narrative

grammar: 〜たままに means 'just as it is / following.' 感じたままに = 'just as you feel it.' 物語 (story) is a recurring motif in this game — Tidus frames life as a story that must be actively driven.

text: キバリが死んだら / 誰がユーナを守るのだ
translation: If Kimahri dies, who will protect Yuna?
grammar: 〜たら is a conditional ('if Kimahri dies'). 誰が〜のだ is a challenging rhetorical question. Kimahri speaks of himself in the third person, as is characteristic of his speech pattern.

text: 私やっちゃうよ
translation: I'm going to do it!

vocabulary.meaning: to do, to go ahead and do
to end up doing (colloquial contraction of てしまう)

grammar: やっちゃう = やってしまう — in this context it has a defiant, determined nuance ('I'm going ahead and doing it!'). Rikku's energetic, reckless personality comes through.

text: ユーナルスカさん戦うってのか / 情がきついぜ
translation: Are you saying we're fighting Yunalesca? / That's rough on a guy.

vocabulary.meaning: here: 情がきつい — emotionally tough, hard to take

grammar: ってのか is a rough masculine form for asking/confirming information ('you mean to say ~?'). 情がきつい is Wakka's earthy way of saying 'this is emotionally brutal.' ぜ is a masculine assertion particle.

text: じゃあ逃げる
translation: Then let's run.
grammar: Plain present tense 逃げる used as a suggestion/decision. Tidus's willingness to just run — defying the sacred site — signals the party's complete rejection of Yunalesca's authority.

text: ここで逃げちゃう / ほら、俺を許せにいな
translation: We'll get out of here. / Hey, forgive me for this!
grammar: 逃げちゃう = 逃げてしまう, colloquial. 俺を許せにいな — a rough, humorous apology (いな is dialectal/archaic for よ or ね in some registers). Tidus is almost joking even in this tense moment — his characteristic lightness.

text: たとえ死んだってな
translation: Even if we die, you know.

vocabulary.meaning: even so, you know (colloquial trailing emphasis)

grammar: たとえ〜ても is a strong concessive ('even if X happens'). って here is a colloquial connector, and な softens the ending. The line trails — the implication is 'even if we die, it's better than giving in.'

text: 同じこと考えてた?
translation: Were you thinking the same thing?

vocabulary.meaning: past progressive (colloquial contraction of ていた)

grammar: 考えてた is past progressive: 'were thinking.' The question has no subject specified — context makes clear Tidus is asking Yuna if she was thinking the same as him (of fighting on, even at the cost of their lives).

text: 言うな! / 一緒に続けよう / 俺たちの物語をさ
translation: Don't say it! / Let's keep going together. / Our story, you know.
grammar: 言うな is the plain prohibitive (dictionary form + な). 〜よう is the volitional ('let's'). さ at the end is a casual emphasis/softening particle. Tidus interrupts Yuna before she can say something final — he refuses to let the story end.

text: 私が消えれば究極召喚は失われる
translation: If I disappear, the Final Summoning will be lost.

vocabulary.meaning: to be lost, to be destroyed (passive)

grammar: 〜えば is a conditional ('if I disappear'). 失われる is the passive of 失う — 'will be lost.' Yunalesca, defeated, declares the consequence of her death: the tool of salvation is gone.

text: あなた方はスピラの希望を消し去ったのです
translation: You have extinguished Spira's hope.

vocabulary.meaning: to completely erase, to wipe out

grammar: 消し去る is a compound verb: 消す (erase) + 去る (go away/remove entirely) — more absolute than 消す alone. のです gives the statement the weight of an accusation or solemn pronouncement. Yunalesca's dying condemnation.

text: だから他の方法を探すんだよ / 愚かな…そのような方法などありません
translation: That's exactly why we'll find another way. / Foolish… No such method exists.

vocabulary.meaning: to search for, to look for

grammar: 〜んだよ (= のだよ) gives the statement warm assertive emphasis — Tidus explaining his intent. そのような〜などありません: など adds dismissiveness ('there is no such thing as that kind of method').

text: たとえあったとしても…万一シーンを倒せても…
translation: Even if such a way existed… even if by some miracle you defeat Sin…

vocabulary.meaning: by some slim chance, on the off chance

grammar: たとえ〜としても is a strong concessive: 'even granting that.' 万一 emphasizes extreme unlikeliness. 〜ても is another concessive. Yunalesca's dying words are a final attempt to extinguish their hope.

text: 永久に生きるエヴォンジュが新たなシーンを生み出すのみ…
translation: Yu Yevon, who lives eternally, will only create a new Sin…

vocabulary.meaning: to produce, to create, to give birth to

grammar: のみ is a literary equivalent of だけ ('only'). Yunalesca reveals Yu Yevon as the true source of Sin — not just a cycle of summoners, but an immortal will that will always regenerate Sin. This is a crucial plot revelation.

text: ああ…ゼンオン…許してください
translation: Ah… Zaon… please forgive me.
grammar: 〜てください is a polite request ('please forgive me'). Zaon is Yunalesca's husband — the first fayth. Her dying words are not defiance but grief: she maintained the cycle for a thousand years out of love and guilt, and now asks his forgiveness.

text: 希望の光を失って…スピラは悲しみの螺旋に落ちる…
translation: Having lost the light of hope… Spira will fall into a spiral of sorrow…
grammar: 〜を失って is the て-form of 失う, indicating cause: 'having lost ~.' 悲しみの螺旋 — 'spiral of sorrow' — is Yunalesca's final prophecy. The word 螺旋 (spiral) echoes the game's title: Final Fantasy X's Japanese subtitle theme of spiraling sorrow.

text: とんでもないこと…しちゃったのかな?
translation: Did we just do something terrible…?

vocabulary.meaning: ended up doing (colloquial past of してしまった)
I wonder if…; uncertain question to oneself

grammar: しちゃった = してしまった — carrying the nuance of 'done and can't be undone.' のかな expresses anxious self-questioning. The party is in shock, uncertain whether they've saved Spira or doomed it.

text: もっととんでもないこと…しよう / どんな?
translation: Let's do something even more outrageous. / Like what?
grammar: しよう is the plain volitional ('let's do'). Tidus pivots from doubt to determination with dark humor — if they've already done something unthinkable, they might as well go further. It's one of his most characteristic moments.

text: シンを倒す、究極召喚なしで / しかも復活させないように
translation: Defeat Sin — without the Final Summoning. / And make sure it doesn't come back.

vocabulary.meaning: moreover, and on top of that
to cause revival (causative of 復活する)

grammar: なしで = without. しかも adds an additional condition on top of the already impossible task. 〜ないように is a purpose/instruction pattern ('so that it does not ~'). The party's impossible new goal, stated plainly.

text: どうやってって、聞くなよな
translation: Don't ask me how, okay?
grammar: どうやってって — the って after どうやって quotes the implied question ('as for asking how'). 聞くな is a plain prohibitive. よな softens it slightly — Tidus admits he has no plan but refuses to be stopped by that.

text: 話がある / 何だよ
translation: I need to talk to you. / What is it?

vocabulary.meaning: I have something to tell you, we need to talk

grammar: 話がある is a set phrase for initiating a serious conversation ('there is talk to be had'). 何だよ — the よ adds rough impatience. Auron and Tidus in a private exchange, the emotional climax of Auron's revelation coming.

text: そろそろ、はっきりさせておこう
translation: It's about time I made this clear.

vocabulary.meaning: to cause to be done (and leave it that way); to get something settled

grammar: そろそろ indicates it's the right moment to act. はっきりさせる = 'to make clear.' 〜ておく means to do something in advance or to settle it. Auron has chosen this moment to finally reveal the truth about himself.

text: そっか。やっぱ、あんたも。
translation: I see. I thought so — you too, huh.

vocabulary.meaning: I see, is that so (casual realization)
as I thought, just as expected (colloquial やはり)

grammar: やっぱ = やはり, expressing that something confirmed a prior suspicion. あんたも — 'you too' implies Tidus already knew about others (his father) and now realizes Auron shares that status. The ellipsis conveys quiet shock.

text: ああ。俺も死人だ。もっと驚くと思ったが。
translation: Yeah. I'm one of the unsent too. I thought you'd be more surprised.

vocabulary.meaning: dead person, the deceased; here: unsent spirit
to be surprised, to be astonished

grammar: 死人だ — blunt, declarative. もっと驚くと思ったが — 〜と思う is indirect quotation ('I thought that ~'). The が at the end is concessive ('but [you weren't]'). Auron's dry admission carries no melodrama.

text: なんか、そんな気してたんだ。
translation: I kind of had a feeling, you know.

vocabulary.meaning: to have a feeling, to sense

grammar: なんか softens the statement ('sort of'). そんな気してた = そんな気がしていた ('I had been having that feeling'). Tidus's calm acceptance of Auron's revelation — he'd sensed it. The moment is understated and deeply human.

text: ユーナ・レスカにやられたんだろう。
translation: It was Yunalesca who killed you, wasn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: to be done in, to be killed, to be defeated (passive/colloquial)
I suppose, that's what happened, right? (conjecture with understanding)

grammar: やられた is the past passive of やる in its violent sense — 'to be taken out/killed.' んだろう = のだろう, expressing inference/conjecture. Tidus pieces together the story: Auron died at Yunalesca's hands ten years ago, and has been an unsent ever since.
